title: Would Uptime Monitoring Catch It?
instruction: Your dashboards track errors, latency and uptime. Would they notice this?

items.text: The recommendation API starts returning HTTP 500 errors
items.why: Errors are exactly what uptime checks watch.

items.text: Response time jumps from 80 ms to 2 seconds
The server runs out of memory and restarts
items.why: Crashes and restarts show up in every health dashboard.

items.text: A feature pipeline stalls; the model keeps serving yesterday's features, with HTTP 200
items.why: Everything is 'up'. The answers are just stale.

items.text: Over six weeks, everyone's top 10 converges on the same 50 items
items.why: A feedback loop: the model trains on its own output. Track catalogue coverage and concentration.

items.text: A catalogue import sets every price to 0 and the deals row fills with broken items
items.why: Valid responses, wrong content. It takes data-quality checks to catch this.

items.text: Clicks stay flat while returns and 'Not interested' taps climb
items.why: The click dashboard looks healthy and no request fails. The damage shows only in outcome signals like returns and rejections, often weeks later.

items.text: Tastes shift after the holiday season; last month's model is slightly wrong every day
items.why: Drift in a world that keeps changing: no error is ever thrown.

debrief: A recommender can answer every request with HTTP 200 and still be broken. Monitor what it recommends, not only whether it answers.
